name: Glendo State Park (Indian Point Campground)
note: Indian Point sits on a peninsula on the east side of Glendo Reservoir, two miles out a gravel road that turns right just before the Sandy Beach fee booth. Its undeveloped sites lie in three areas off two-track dirt lanes, which the park says suit medium-sized units or tents: IP01-IP12 along the edge of a cottonwood stand (the first six without shade), a group site by the boat ramp, and IP17-IP20 a short way up the dirt road toward Broken Arrow, a road the park says has sandy stretches that heavy rain can make impassable. The lake reaches the edge of the campground only at high water (late spring to early summer); as the reservoir drops the shore recedes across bare flats. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: reserve.wyoming.gov (US eDirect API wyordr.usedirect.com/wyomingrdr/rdr/, PlaceId 10 'Glendo State Park', FacilityId 338 'Indian Point', facility point 42.53522,-104.95278, read 2026-11-20): 17 web-bookable units - 16 'Campsite Non-Electric' IP01-IP12 and IP17-IP20 (IsRVSite true, 'Unit & Parking Size(ft)' 40-160 (IP01 40, IP08 45, the rest 60-160), 'Parking Pad Material: None' (natural ground), PullInTypeName 'Not Applicable', Rate 10.00, MaximumStay 14) + Group Site IP13 ('Sites included: 13, 14, 15, 16') -> real drive-in RV campground a 23-ft rig fits. Wyoming State Parks' own Indian Point page (wyoparks.wyo.gov/index.php/about-our-campgrounds/1695-indian-point-glendo, read as search-result text 2026-11-20; the site refuses with an F5 challenge) and its copies on The Dyrt and Campflare (read 2026-11-20): 21 campsites in three areas, 'All sites in this campground are undeveloped, with two-track dirt roads for access', 'best suited to medium sized camping units, or tents'; reached by Glendo Park Road to the Sandy Beach turn-off, then 'Just before the Sandy Beach fee booth, turn right on the gravel road and follow it two miles to Indian Point.' No 4WD or sand wording on Indian Point's own page; the Broken Arrow page's 4WD recommendation (lead 15) covers 'The access road to reach Broken Arrow after the Indian Point Ramp', i.e. beyond this campground's ramp - IP17-IP20 sit on a spur ~150-250 m along that road (imagery), so they carry a caveat, while IP01-IP13 lie before the ramp on the gravel road. Imagery 2026-11-20: red gravel road to the ramp, sites on grass/dirt flats off short two-track loops, vault-toilet buildings by the ramp lot and the IP17-IP20 loop. Not in the DB: no WY name match (1887 Indian Point is MO, 5105 MS); nearest entries 15738 Cottonwood ~1.1 km (FacilityId 335) and 13976 Sandy Beach ~2 km, separate facilities. Public (state): no price gate.

flags: Access: Indian Point's own page has no 4WD or sand wording - only 'two-track dirt roads' and 'best suited to medium sized camping units, or tents' (a 23-ft rig is medium). But IP17-IP20 are reached ~150-250 m along the dirt road past the Indian Point Ramp toward Broken Arrow, the road whose page says it has 'several sandy areas', can become impassable after heavy precipitation, and recommends 4WD for Broken Arrow (lead 15 skipped on it). Kept with the caveat in the note; IP01-IP13 lie before the ramp off the gravel road. If AWH reads the Broken Arrow wording as covering the whole road past the ramp, IP17-IP20 (including two of the four waterfront sites) drop out and the entry stays on IP01-IP13.

Waterfront: lakefront on four clear sites (IP02, IP03 at the east end; IP19, IP20 on the north loop), each ~25-45 m from the full-pool contour over open ground (lidar + imagery). Contrary claim: the park's description (via The Dyrt's copy) says cottonwoods and thick underbrush separate sites 1-6 from the shoreline - true of the drawn-down summer shore and of IP04-IP06, but the lidar's own water surface (flown ~0.5 m below full pool) stands 25-30 m from IP03 across a bare apron. If the reviewer weighs the park's wording over the lidar, lakeview is the fallback.

Season of the water: Glendo draws down hard (47% on 2025-01-30 per the park page); the boat ramp is 'normally open and usable from early May to late July' (park text via The Dyrt). Full pool reaches the lakefront sites only around late spring - early summer.
